units: Sabb. 53ᵇ, v. פָּרַךְ.—Esp. to grind colors, rub with paint, paint (hair, skin); trnsf. to give a deceptive appearance to.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2">Lam. R. to II, 1</cite> <he>והיו … מְפַרְכְּסִין בדם וכ׳</he> and the men of the country painted (themselves) with the blood of his (the king’s) enemies.

<cite ref="Shabbat 34a:2">Sabb. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>זונות מפַרְכְּסוֹת זו את זו וכ׳</he> harlots paint one another, how much the more must scholars (be regardful of one another’s honor)! <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:12">B. Mets. IV, 12</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 60a:14">60ᵃ</cite>) <he>אין מְפַרְכְּסִין לא את האדם וכ׳</he> (Y. ed. a. Mish. Nap. <he>מְפַרְקְסִין</he>) you must not give a deceptive appearance to a human being (slave to be sold) or to a beast or to vessels, v. <cite ref="Q00859"><he>פִּירְכּוּס</he> I</cite>. Y. ib. IV, end, 9ᵈ <he>מהו אין מפרקסין … צור גרמך</he> what is meant by ‘you must not paint (a slave)’? You must not tell him, paint thyself (to appear younger); a. e.
